sentences.zh: 夫不言而信，天之道也。

translations.literal: Not speaking yet being trusted—this is the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: To speak without words yet be trusted—such is the Way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天於人君有告戒之道焉，示之以象而已。

translations.literal: Heaven has a way of admonishing human rulers: it simply displays signs to them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven holds a way of warning and admonishing the ruler of men: it merely reveals signs to him.

sentences.zh: 故自上古以來，天文有世掌之官，唐虞羲、和，夏昆吾，商巫咸，周史佚、甘德、石申之流。

translations.literal: Thus from high antiquity onward, astronomy has had hereditary officers: Xi and He under Tang and Yu, Kunwu under Xia, Wuxian under Shang, and under Zhou such men as Shiyu, Gande, and Shishen.
translations.idiomatic: From highest antiquity, therefore, astronomy has had officers who held the office by hereditary succession—Xi and He under Tang and Yu, Kunwu under Xia, Wuxian under Shang, and under Zhou such figures as Shiyu, Gande, and Shishen.

sentences.zh: 居是官者，專察天象之常變，而述天心告戒之意，進言於其君，以致交修之儆焉。

translations.literal: Those who held this office devoted themselves to observing the regular and changing phenomena of heaven, expounded the meaning of Heaven's heart in warning and admonition, and presented their words to their ruler, so as to bring about mutual cultivation and vigilance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held this office were charged solely with observing the regular and anomalous signs of heaven, with setting forth the intent of Heaven's warnings, and with advising their sovereign—so that ruler and ministers might together cultivate virtue and remain vigilant.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，見吉凶，聖人則之。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: 'Heaven hangs forth its signs, revealing fortune and misfortune, and the sage takes them as his model.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: 'Heaven displays its signs, revealing good and ill fortune, and the sage takes them as his standard.'

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「觀乎天文，以察時變。

translations.literal: It also says: 'Observe the patterns of heaven to examine the changes of the seasons.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'Contemplate the patterns of heaven to discern the changes of the seasons.'

sentences.zh: 」是也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the meaning.

sentences.zh: 然考《堯典》，中星不過正人時以興民事。

translations.literal: Yet when one examines the Canon of Yao, the culminating stars served only to set the seasons aright and promote the people's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when one examines the Canon of Yao, the culminating stars served only to correct the seasons and advance the people's labors.

sentences.zh: 夏仲康之世，《胤征》之篇：「乃季秋月朔，辰弗集于房。

translations.literal: In the age of Zhongkang of Xia, the Punitive Expedition states: 'On the first day of the last month of autumn, the stars did not gather in Fang.'
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Zhongkang of Xia, the Punitive Expedition on Zhong reads: 'On the first day of the last month of autumn, the stars did not gather in Fang.'

sentences.zh: 」然後日食之變昉見於《書》。

translations.literal: Only then did the anomaly of solar eclipse first appear in the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the phenomenon of solar eclipse first appear in the Documents.

sentences.zh: 觀其數羲、和以「俶擾天紀」、「昏迷天象」之罪而討之，則知先王克謹天戒，所以責成于司天之官者，豈輕任哉！

translations.literal: When one sees how the two Xi and He were punished on charges of 'disrupting the celestial order' and 'confusing the heavenly signs,' one knows that the former kings strictly heeded Heaven's warnings—how could the responsibility entrusted to officers of heaven have been a light charge!
translations.idiomatic: When one sees how the two Xi and He were punished for the crimes of 'disturbing the celestial order' and 'confounding the heavenly signs,' one understands that the ancient kings took Heaven's warnings with utmost seriousness—how could the charge laid upon officers of heaven have been a light one!

translations.literal: Not speaking yet being trusted—this is the Way of Heaven. Heaven has a way of admonishing human rulers: it simply displays signs to them. Thus from high antiquity onward, astronomy has had hereditary officers: Xi and He under Tang and Yu, Kunwu under Xia, Wuxian under Shang, and under Zhou such men as Shiyu, Gande, and Shishen. Those who held this office devoted themselves to observing the regular and changing phenomena of heaven, expounded the meaning of Heaven's heart in warning and admonition, and presented their words to their ruler, so as to bring about mutual cultivation and vigilance. The Book of Changes says: 'Heaven hangs forth its signs, revealing fortune and misfortune, and the sage takes them as his model.' It also says: 'Observe the patterns of heaven to examine the changes of the seasons.' This is what is meant. Yet when one examines the Canon of Yao, the culminating stars served only to set the seasons aright and promote the people's affairs. In the age of Zhongkang of Xia, the Punitive Expedition states: 'On the first day of the last month of autumn, the stars did not gather in Fang.' Only then did the anomaly of solar eclipse first appear in the Documents. When one sees how the two Xi and He were punished on charges of 'disrupting the celestial order' and 'confusing the heavenly signs,' one knows that the former kings strictly heeded Heaven's warnings—how could the responsibility entrusted to officers of heaven have been a light charge!

Those who held this office were charged solely with observing the regular and anomalous signs of heaven, with setting forth the intent of Heaven's warnings, and with advising their sovereign—so that ruler and ministers might together cultivate virtue and remain vigilant. It also says: 'Contemplate the patterns of heaven to discern the changes of the seasons.' Such is the meaning. Yet when one examines the Canon of Yao, the culminating stars served only to correct the seasons and advance the people's labors. In the reign of Zhongkang of Xia, the Punitive Expedition on Zhong reads: 'On the first day of the last month of autumn, the stars did not gather in Fang.' Only then did the phenomenon of solar eclipse first appear in the Documents. When one sees how the two Xi and He were punished for the crimes of 'disturbing the celestial order' and 'confounding the heavenly signs,' one understands that the ancient kings took Heaven's warnings with utmost seriousness—how could the charge laid upon officers of heaven have been a light one!

sentences.zh: 箕子《洪範》論休咎之征曰：「王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日。

translations.literal: Jizi in the Great Plan, discussing the signs of blessing and calamity, says: 'The king examines by the year, ministers and grandees by the month, masters and chiefs by the day.'

translations.literal: 'The common people are examined by the stars; stars have their preference for wind, stars have their preference for rain.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The common people are examined by the stars; stars have their preference for wind, and stars have their preference for rain.'

sentences.zh: 」《禮記》言體信達順之效，則以天降膏露先之。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites, in speaking of the effects of embodying trust and achieving accord, takes the descent of sweet dew from heaven as the first sign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Book of Rites speaks of the effects of embodying trust and achieving harmony, it takes the descent of sweet dew from heaven as the first sign.

sentences.zh: 至於周《詩》，屢言天變，所謂「旻天疾威，敷於下土」，又所謂「雨無其極，傷我稼穡」，「正月繁霜，我心憂傷」，以及「彼月而微，此日而微」，「燁燁震電，不寧不令」。

translations.literal: As for the Odes of Zhou, they repeatedly speak of heavenly changes—such as 'Ministering Heaven is fierce in wrath, spreading over the lower realm'; also 'The rain knows no limit, injuring our grain'; 'In the first month, heavy frost—I am grieved at heart'; as well as 'That moon is faint, this sun is faint,' and 'Flashing lightning, neither peace nor good order.'

sentences.zh: 孔子刪《詩》而存之，以示戒也。

translations.literal: Confucius edited the Odes yet preserved these passages, to show their admonitory purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius edited the Odes yet retained these lines, to show their purpose as warnings.

sentences.zh: 他日約魯史而作《春秋》，則日食、星變屢書而不爲煩。

translations.literal: Later, when he condensed the chronicles of Lu to compose the Spring and Autumn Annals, he recorded solar eclipses and stellar changes repeatedly without deeming it excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he condensed the Lu chronicles to compose the Spring and Autumn Annals, he recorded solar eclipses and stellar changes again and again without finding it excessive.

sentences.zh: 聖人以天道戒謹後世之旨，昭然可睹矣。

translations.literal: The intent of the sages to warn and admonish later ages through the Way of Heaven is plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: The sages' intent to admonish and warn later ages through the Way of Heaven is plainly visible.

sentences.zh: 於是司馬遷《史記》而下，歷代皆志天文。

translations.literal: Thereupon, from Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian onward, every dynasty has included a treatise on astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: From Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian onward, every dynasty has recorded astronomy in its annals.

sentences.zh: 第以羲、和既遠，官乏世掌，賴世以有專門之學焉。

translations.literal: Only because Xi and He were far removed in time and the office lacked hereditary holders, each age came to rely on specialized learning.
translations.idiomatic: Only because Xi and He were far removed in time and the office lacked hereditary holders, each age came to depend on specialized learning.

sentences.zh: 然其說三家：曰周髀，曰宣夜，曰渾天。

translations.literal: Yet there were three schools of theory: the Gnomon of Zhou, the Clarification of Night, and the Armillary Sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there were three schools: the Gnomon of Zhou, the Clarification of Night, and the Armillary Sphere.

sentences.zh: 宣夜先絕，周髀多差，渾天之學遭秦而滅，洛下閎、耿壽昌晚出，始物色得之。

translations.literal: The Clarification of Night died out first; the Gnomon of Zhou had many errors; the Armillary Sphere tradition was extinguished under Qin—Luoxia Hong and Geng Shouchang appeared only later and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: The Clarification of Night perished first; the Gnomon of Zhou was often in error; the Armillary Sphere tradition was lost under Qin—Luoxia Hong and Geng Shouchang appeared only later and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 故自魏、晉以至隋、唐，精天文之學者犖犖名世，豈世難得其人歟！

translations.literal: Thus from Wei and Jin through Sui and Tang, masters of astronomy stood out in every generation—was it truly that the age could not find such men!
translations.idiomatic: Thus from Wei and Jin through Sui and Tang, masters of astronomy distinguished themselves in every generation—was it truly that the age could not find such men!

sentences.zh: 宋之初興，近臣如楚昭輔，文臣如竇儀，號知天文。

translations.literal: At the founding of Song, close ministers such as Chu Zhaofu and civil officials such as Dou Yi were reputed to know astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Song, close ministers such as Chu Zhaofu and civil officials such as Dou Yi were reputed to know astronomy.

sentences.zh: 太宗之世，召天下伎術有能明天文者，試隸司天臺；

translations.literal: In the reign of Taizong, all those throughout the realm skilled in techniques who could understand astronomy were summoned and tested for appointment to the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Taizong, all throughout the realm who were skilled in techniques and could understand astronomy were summoned and tested for appointment to the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 匿不以聞者幻罪論死。

translations.literal: Those who concealed their ability and did not report it were sentenced to death on a charge of sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: Those who concealed their ability and did not report it were sentenced to death on a charge of sorcery.

sentences.zh: 既而張思訓、韓顯符輩以推步進。

translations.literal: Thereafter Zhang Sixun, Han Xianfu, and their like advanced through calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Zhang Sixun, Han Xianfu, and their like advanced through calendrical calculation.

sentences.zh: 其後學士大夫如沈括之議，蘇頌之作，亦皆底於幻眇。

translations.literal: Later, learned officials and grandees such as Shen Kuo in his memorials and Su Song in his constructions all reached the subtlest depths.
translations.idiomatic: Later, learned officials and grandees such as Shen Kuo in his memorials and Su Song in his constructions all attained the subtlest depths.

sentences.zh: 靖康之變，測驗之器盡歸金人。

translations.literal: At the Jingkang disaster, all instruments of observation passed to the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jingkang disaster, all instruments of observation passed to the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，至紹興十三年，始因秘書丞嚴抑之請，命太史局重創渾儀。

translations.literal: After Gaozong crossed south, down to the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, at the request of Secretary Assistant Yan Yi, the Bureau of Astronomy was ordered to recreate the armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong crossed south, down to the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, at the request of Secretary Assistant Yan Yi, the Bureau of Astronomy was ordered to recreate the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 自是厥後，窺測占候蓋不廢焉爾。

translations.literal: From that time onward, observation and divination were never abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward, observation and divination were never abandoned.

sentences.zh: 甯宗慶元四年九月，太史言月食於晝，草澤上書言食於夜。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Qingyuan under Ningzong, the Grand Astrologer said the lunar eclipse would occur by day; a commoner submitted a memorial saying it would occur by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Qingyuan under Ningzong, the Grand Astrologer said the lunar eclipse would occur by day; a commoner submitted a memorial saying it would occur by night.

sentences.zh: 及驗視，如草澤言。

translations.literal: When it was verified, it was as the commoner had said.
translations.idiomatic: When it was verified, it was as the commoner had said.

sentences.zh: 乃更造《統天曆》，命秘書正字馮履參定。

translations.literal: Thereupon a new calendar, the Tongtian Calendar, was created, and Secretary Corrector Feng Lü was ordered to assist in its determination.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon a new calendar, the Tongtian Calendar, was created, and Secretary Corrector Feng Lü was ordered to assist in its determination.

sentences.zh: 以是推之，民間天文之學蓋有精于太史者，則太宗召試之法亦豈徒哉！

translations.literal: From this one may infer that among the people there were those whose learning in astronomy surpassed that of the Grand Astrologer—so Taizong's method of summoning and testing was not in vain!
translations.idiomatic: From this one may infer that among the people there were those whose learning in astronomy surpassed that of the Grand Astrologer—so Taizong's method of summoning and testing was not in vain!

sentences.zh: 今東都舊史所書天文禎祥、日月薄蝕、五緯淩犯、彗孛飛流、暈珥虹霓、精祲雲氣等事，其言時日災祥之應，分野休咎之別，視南渡後史有詳略焉。

translations.literal: Now the Eastern Capital's old histories record such matters as celestial omens, solar and lunar eclipses, encroachments of the five planets, comets and broom-stars, meteors, halos and coronae, rainbows, strange vapors, and cloud formations; in speaking of the correspondence of auspice and calamity to time and day, and the distinction of fortune and misfortune by territorial division, the histories after the Southern Crossing differ in detail and brevity.
translations.idiomatic: The old histories of the Eastern Capital record such matters as celestial omens, solar and lunar eclipses, encroachments of the five planets, comets and broom-stars, meteors, halos and coronae, rainbows, strange vapors, and cloud formations; in speaking of the correspondence of auspice and calamity to time and day, and the distinction of fortune and misfortune by territorial division, the histories after the Southern Crossing differ in detail and brevity.

sentences.zh: 蓋東都之日，海內爲一人，君遇變修德，無或他諉。

translations.literal: For in the days of the Eastern Capital, all within the seas were one people; when the ruler encountered change he cultivated virtue, and none shifted blame elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: For in the days of the Eastern Capital, all within the seas were one people; when the ruler encountered change he cultivated virtue, and none shifted blame elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 南渡土宇分裂，太史所上，必謹星野之書。

translations.literal: After the Southern Crossing the realm was divided; what the Grand Astrologer submitted had to observe carefully the books of stellar territories.
translations.idiomatic: After the Southern Crossing the realm was divided; what the Grand Astrologer submitted had to observe carefully the books of stellar territories.

sentences.zh: 且君臣恐懼修省之余，故于天文休咎之應有不容不縷述而申言之者，是亦時勢使然，未可以言星翁、日官之術有精粗敬怠之不同也。

translations.literal: Moreover, beyond the fear and self-examination of ruler and ministers, there were responses of heavenly blessing and calamity that could not but be set forth in detail—this too was compelled by the times; one cannot say that the arts of star-readers and day-officers differed in refinement, coarseness, reverence, or negligence.

sentences.zh: 今合累朝史臣所錄爲一志，而取歐陽修《新唐書》、《五代史記》爲法，凡征驗之說有涉于傅會，鹹削而不書，歸於傳信而已矣。

translations.literal: Now the records of successive dynasties' historians are combined into one treatise, taking Ouyang Xiu's New Book of Tang and Records of the Five Dynasties as models; wherever verification theories involve forced correspondence, all are cut out and not written—returning to faithful transmission alone.

In the reign of Taizong, all those throughout the realm skilled in techniques who could understand astronomy were summoned and tested for appointment to the Directorate of Astronomy. Later, learned officials and grandees such as Shen Kuo in his memorials and Su Song in his constructions all reached the subtlest depths. When it was verified, it was as the commoner had said. Thereupon a new calendar, the Tongtian Calendar, was created, and Secretary Corrector Feng Lü was ordered to assist in its determination. translations.literal: Fifth, the leveling wheel: above the water level, diameter six chi one cun three fen, circumference one zhang eight chi three cun nine fen; the Eight Trigrams, ten stems, twelve branches, twenty-four qi, and seventy-two hou are carved within; it fixes the four dimensions and day-hours, and corrects the hundred quarters of day and night.

sentences.zh: 六曰黃道，南北各去赤道二十四度，東西交於卯酉，以爲日行盈縮、月行九道之限。

translations.literal: Sixth, the ecliptic: north and south each 24 degrees from the equator, east and west crossing at mao and you, serving as the limit of the sun's expansion and contraction and the moon's nine paths.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the ecliptic: north and south each 24 degrees from the equator, east and west crossing at mao and you, serving as the limit of the sun's expansion and contraction and the moon's nine paths.

sentences.zh: 凡冬至日行南極，去北極一百一十五度，故景長而寒；

translations.literal: At the winter solstice the sun travels to the south pole, 115 degrees from the north pole, so the shadow is long and it is cold.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice the sun travels to the south pole, 115 degrees from the north pole, so the shadow is long and it is cold.

sentences.zh: 夏至日在赤道北二十四度，去北極六十七度，故景短而暑。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice the sun is 24 degrees north of the equator, 67 degrees from the north pole, so the shadow is short and it is hot.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice the sun is 24 degrees north of the equator, 67 degrees from the north pole, so the shadow is short and it is hot.

sentences.zh: 月有九道之行，歲匝十二辰，正交出入黃道，遠不過六度。

translations.literal: The moon has nine paths of travel; each year it circles the twelve branches; at direct crossing it enters and exits the ecliptic, never exceeding six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The moon has nine paths of travel; each year it circles the twelve branches; at direct crossing it enters and exits the ecliptic, never exceeding six degrees.

sentences.zh: 五星順、留、伏、逆行度之常數也。

translations.literal: These are the regular numbers of the five planets' direct motion, station, hiding, and retrograde degrees.
translations.idiomatic: These are the regular numbers of the five planets' direct motion, station, hiding, and retrograde degrees.

sentences.zh: 七曰赤道，與黃道等，帶天之紘以隔黃道，去兩極各九十一度強。

translations.literal: Seventh, the equator: equal to the ecliptic, girding heaven's cord to separate the ecliptic, 91-odd degrees from each pole.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the equator: equal to the ecliptic, girding heaven's cord to separate the ecliptic, 91-odd degrees from each pole.

sentences.zh: 黃道之交也，按經東交角宿五度少，西交奎宿一十四度強。

translations.literal: At the ecliptic's crossing: according to the classics, the eastern crossing is at Horn 5-odd degrees, the western at Straddle 14-odd degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At the ecliptic's crossing: according to the classics, the eastern crossing is at Horn 5-odd degrees, the western at Straddle 14-odd degrees.

sentences.zh: 日出於赤道外，遠不過二十四度。

translations.literal: The sun rises outside the equator, never exceeding 24 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The sun rises outside the equator, never exceeding 24 degrees.

sentences.zh: 冬至之日行鬥宿，日入於赤道內，亦不過二十四度，夏至之日行井宿；

translations.literal: On the day of the winter solstice it travels at Dipper; the sun sets within the equator, also not exceeding 24 degrees; on the day of the summer solstice it travels at Well.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the winter solstice it travels at Dipper; the sun sets within the equator, also not exceeding 24 degrees; on the day of the summer solstice it travels at Well.

sentences.zh: 及晝夜分，炎涼等。

translations.literal: At the division of day and night, heat and coolness are equal.
translations.idiomatic: At the division of day and night, heat and coolness are equal.

sentences.zh: 日、月、五星陰陽進退盈縮之常數也。

translations.literal: These are the regular numbers of yin and yang advance, retreat, expansion, and contraction for sun, moon, and five planets.
translations.idiomatic: These are the regular numbers of yin and yang advance, retreat, expansion, and contraction for sun, moon, and five planets.

sentences.zh: 八曰龍柱，四，各高五尺五寸，並于平准輪下。

translations.literal: Eighth, the dragon pillars: four, each five chi five cun high, all beneath the leveling wheel.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the dragon pillars: four, each five chi five cun high, all beneath the leveling wheel.

translations.literal: Eighth, the dragon pillars: four, each five chi five cun high, all beneath the leveling wheel.

sentences.zh: 九曰水臬，十字爲之，其水準滿，北辰正。

translations.literal: Ninth, the water level: made in the form of a cross; when its water is full, the north star is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, the water level: made in the form of a cross; when its water is full, the north star is correct.

sentences.zh: 以置四隅，各長七尺五寸，高三寸半，深一寸。

translations.literal: Four corners are set, each seven chi five cun long, three cun half high, one cun deep.
translations.idiomatic: Four corners are set, each seven chi five cun long, three cun half high, one cun deep.

sentences.zh: 四隅水準則天地准。

translations.literal: When the four corners' water levels are correct, heaven and earth are level.
translations.idiomatic: When the four corners' water levels are correct, heaven and earth are level.

translations.literal: Ninth, the water level: made in the form of a cross; when its water is full, the north star is correct. Four corners are set, each seven chi five cun long, three cun half high, one cun deep. When the four corners' water levels are correct, heaven and earth are level.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀初，李淳風於浚儀縣古嶽台測北極出地高三十四度八分，差陽城四分。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan in Tang, Li Chunfeng at the ancient Yue Terrace in Junyi County measured the north pole 34 degrees 8 fen above earth, differing from Yangcheng by 4 fen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan in Tang, Li Chunfeng at the ancient Yue Terrace in Junyi County measured the north pole 34 degrees 8 fen above earth, differing from Yangcheng by 4 fen.

sentences.zh: 今測定北極高三十五度以爲常准。

translations.literal: Now the north pole height is determined at 35 degrees as the constant standard.
translations.idiomatic: Now the north pole height is determined at 35 degrees as the constant standard.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年七月，沈括上《渾儀》、《浮漏》、《景表》三議。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year of Xining, Shen Kuo submitted three memorials: On the Armillary Sphere, On the Clepsydra, and On the Gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year of Xining, Shen Kuo submitted three memorials: On the Armillary Sphere, On the Clepsydra, and On the Gnomon.

sentences.zh: 《渾儀議》曰：

translations.literal: The Memorial on the Armillary Sphere says:
translations.idiomatic: The Memorial on the Armillary Sphere says:

sentences.zh: 五星之行有疾舒，日月之交有見匿，求其次舍經劘之會，其法一寓於日。

translations.literal: The five planets' motion has swiftness and slowness; the sun and moon's crossing has visibility and concealment; to seek their lodges and the meetings of longitude and latitude, the method all resides in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The five planets' motion has swiftness and slowness; the sun and moon's crossing has visibility and concealment; to seek their lodges and the meetings of longitude and latitude, the method all resides in the sun.

sentences.zh: 冬至之日，日之端南者也。

translations.literal: The day of the winter solstice is the day when the sun's tip is southernmost.
translations.idiomatic: The day of the winter solstice is the day when the sun's tip is southernmost.

sentences.zh: 日行周天而復集於表銳，凡三百六十有五日四分日之幾一，而謂之歲。

translations.literal: The sun travels the full circuit of heaven and again gathers at the gnomon's point—altogether 365 and a fraction of a day—and this is called a year.
translations.idiomatic: The sun travels the full circuit of heaven and again gathers at the gnomon's point—altogether 365 and a fraction of a day—and this is called a year.

sentences.zh: 周天之體，日別之謂之度。

translations.literal: The body of the full circuit of heaven, divided by the sun, is called a degree.
translations.idiomatic: The body of the full circuit of heaven, divided by the sun, is called a degree.

sentences.zh: 度之離，其數有二：日行則舒則疾，會而均，別之曰赤道之度；

translations.literal: The separation of degrees has two numbers: when the sun travels it is slow then swift, meeting and averaging—this is separately called equatorial degree.
translations.idiomatic: The separation of degrees has two numbers: when the sun travels it is slow then swift, meeting and averaging—this is separately called equatorial degree.

sentences.zh: 日行自南而北，升降四十有八度而迤，別之曰黃道之度。

translations.literal: When the sun travels from south to north, rising and falling 48 degrees in winding course, this is separately called ecliptic degree.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun travels from south to north, rising and falling 48 degrees in winding course, this is separately called ecliptic degree.

sentences.zh: 度不可見，其可見者星也。

translations.literal: Degrees cannot be seen; what can be seen are stars.
translations.idiomatic: Degrees cannot be seen; what can be seen are stars.

sentences.zh: 日、月、五星之所由，有星焉。

translations.literal: Where sun, moon, and five planets pass, there are stars.
translations.idiomatic: Where sun, moon, and five planets pass, there are stars.

sentences.zh: 當度之畫者凡二十有八，而謂之舍。

translations.literal: Those that mark the degrees are 28 in all, and are called lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Those that mark the degrees are 28 in all, and are called lodges.

sentences.zh: 舍所以絜度，度所以生數也。

translations.literal: Lodges are what bind degrees; degrees are what generate numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Lodges are what bind degrees; degrees are what generate numbers.

sentences.zh: 度在天者也，爲之璣衡，則度在器。

translations.literal: Degrees are in heaven; make an armillary sphere for them, and degrees are in the instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Degrees are in heaven; make an armillary sphere for them, and degrees are in the instrument.

sentences.zh: 度在器，則日月五星可摶乎器中，而天無所豫也。

translations.literal: When degrees are in the instrument, sun, moon, and five planets can be grasped within the instrument, and heaven need not be anticipated.
translations.idiomatic: When degrees are in the instrument, sun, moon, and five planets can be grasped within the instrument, and heaven need not be anticipated.

sentences.zh: 天無所豫，則在天者不爲難知也。

translations.literal: When heaven need not be anticipated, what is in heaven is not hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven need not be anticipated, what is in heaven is not hard to know.

sentences.zh: 自漢以前，爲曆者必有璣衡以自驗跡。

translations.literal: Before Han, calendar-makers necessarily had armillary spheres to verify their traces.
translations.idiomatic: Before Han, calendar-makers necessarily had armillary spheres to verify their traces.

sentences.zh: 其後雖有璣衡，而不爲曆作。

translations.literal: Afterward, though armillary spheres existed, they were not made for calendar work.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, though armillary spheres existed, they were not made for calendar work.

sentences.zh: 爲曆者亦不復以器自考，氣朔星緯，皆莫能知其必當之數。

translations.literal: Calendar-makers also no longer used instruments to examine themselves; qi, new moon, and stellar longitude—all could not know their necessary corresponding numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-makers also no longer used instruments to examine themselves; qi, new moon, and stellar longitude—all could not know their necessary corresponding numbers.

sentences.zh: 至唐僧一行改《大衍曆法》，始復用渾儀參實，故其術所得，比諸家爲多。

translations.literal: Until the Tang monk Yixing revised the Dayan Calendar Method, only then was the armillary sphere again used to verify reality; therefore his method's results exceeded those of other schools.
translations.idiomatic: Until the Tang monk Yixing revised the Dayan Calendar Method, only then was the armillary sphere again used to verify reality; therefore his method's results exceeded those of other schools.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗曆考古今儀象之法，《虞書》所謂璿璣玉衡，唯鄭康成粗記其法，至洛下閎制圓儀，賈逵又加黃道，其詳皆不存於書。

translations.literal: The Xuanji and Jade Balance spoken of in the Book of Yu—only Zheng Xuan roughly recorded their method; when Luoxia Hong made the circular instrument and Jia Kui added the ecliptic, the details are all not preserved in books.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanji and Jade Balance spoken of in the Book of Yu—only Zheng Xuan roughly recorded their method; when Luoxia Hong made the circular instrument and Jia Kui added the ecliptic, the details are all not preserved in books.

sentences.zh: 其後張衡爲銅儀於密室中，以水轉之，蓋所謂渾象，非古之璣衡也。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhang Heng made a bronze instrument in a sealed chamber, turned by water—this is the so-called celestial globe, not the ancient armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Zhang Heng made a bronze instrument in a sealed chamber, turned by water—this is the so-called celestial globe, not the ancient armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 吳孫氏時王蕃、陸績皆嘗爲儀及象，其說以謂舊以二分爲一度，而患星辰稠穊，張衡改用四分，而復椎重難運。

translations.literal: In the time of Sun of Wu, Wang Fan and Lu Ji both made instruments and globes; their theory held that formerly two fen made one degree, but they worried the stars were too dense; Zhang Heng changed to four fen, but again it was too heavy and hard to turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Sun of Wu, Wang Fan and Lu Ji both made instruments and globes; their theory held that formerly two fen made one degree, but they worried the stars were too dense; Zhang Heng changed to four fen, but again it was too heavy and hard to turn.

sentences.zh: 故蕃以三分爲度，周丈有九寸五分寸之三，而具黃赤道焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Fan used three fen as one degree, circumference one zhang nine cun and three-fifths of a cun, and included both yellow and red equators.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Fan used three fen as one degree, circumference one zhang nine cun and three-fifths of a cun, and included both yellow and red equators.

sentences.zh: 績之說以天形如鳥卵小橢，而黃、赤道短長相害，不能應法。

translations.literal: Ji's theory held that heaven's form is like a bird's egg, slightly oblate, and the yellow and red equators' short and long harm each other, unable to respond to the method.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's theory held that heaven's form is like a bird's egg, slightly oblate, and the yellow and red equators' short and long harm each other, unable to respond to the method.

sentences.zh: 至劉曜時，南陽孔定制銅儀，有雙規，規正距子午以象天；

translations.literal: At the time of Liu Yao, Kong Ding of Nanyang made a bronze instrument with paired rings: the rings upright and distanced from meridian to represent heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Liu Yao, Kong Ding of Nanyang made a bronze instrument with paired rings: the rings upright and distanced from meridian to represent heaven.

sentences.zh: 有橫規，判儀之中以象地；

translations.literal: There was a horizontal ring, dividing the instrument's center to represent earth.
translations.idiomatic: There was a horizontal ring, dividing the instrument's center to represent earth.

sentences.zh: 有時規，斜絡天腹以候赤道；

translations.literal: There was a time ring, slanting across heaven's belly to observe the equator.
translations.idiomatic: There was a time ring, slanting across heaven's belly to observe the equator.

sentences.zh: 南北植幹，以法二極；

translations.literal: North and south upright posts to model the two poles.
translations.idiomatic: North and south upright posts to model the two poles.

sentences.zh: 其中乃爲遊規、窺管。

translations.literal: Within these were the traveling ring and sighting tube.
translations.idiomatic: Within these were the traveling ring and sighting tube.

sentences.zh: 劉曜太史令晁崇、斛蘭皆嘗爲鐵儀，其規有六，四常定，以象地，一象赤道，其二象二極，乃是定所謂雙規者也。

translations.literal: Liu Yao's Grand Astrologer Chao Chong and Hulu both made iron instruments; their rings were six—four constantly fixed to represent earth, one representing the equator, two representing the two poles—this is what fixed the so-called paired rings.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao's Grand Astrologer Chao Chong and Hulu both made iron instruments; their rings were six—four constantly fixed to represent earth, one representing the equator, two representing the two poles—this is what fixed the so-called paired rings.

sentences.zh: 其制與定法大同，唯南北柱曲抱雙規，下有縱衡水平，以銀錯星度，小變舊法。

translations.literal: The construction largely matched Ding's method, only the north and south pillars curved to embrace the paired rings; below were vertical and horizontal levels; star degrees were inlaid in silver—a small change from the old method.
translations.idiomatic: The construction largely matched Ding's method, only the north and south pillars curved to embrace the paired rings; below were vertical and horizontal levels; star degrees were inlaid in silver—a small change from the old method.

sentences.zh: 而皆不言有黃道，疑其失傳也。

translations.literal: Yet none spoke of having an ecliptic—one suspects this was lost in transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Yet none spoke of having an ecliptic—one suspects this was lost in transmission.

sentences.zh: 唐李淳風爲圓儀三重：其外曰六合，有天經雙規、金渾緯規、金常規。

translations.literal: Li Chunfeng of Tang made a triple circular instrument: the outermost called Six Harmonies, with celestial meridian paired rings, golden armillary latitude ring, and golden regular ring.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng of Tang made a triple circular instrument: the outermost called Six Harmonies, with celestial meridian paired rings, golden armillary latitude ring, and golden regular ring.

sentences.zh: 次曰三辰，轉於六合之內，圓徑八尺，有璿璣規、月遊規，所謂璿璣者，黃、赤道屬焉。

translations.literal: Next called Three Luminaries, turning within the Six Harmonies, circular diameter eight chi, with Xuanji ring and moon-traveling ring—the so-called Xuanji has yellow and red equators attached.
translations.idiomatic: Next called Three Luminaries, turning within the Six Harmonies, circular diameter eight chi, with Xuanji ring and moon-traveling ring—the so-called Xuanji has yellow and red equators attached.

sentences.zh: 又次曰四遊，南北爲天樞，中爲遊筒可以升降遊轉，別爲月道，傍列二百四十九交以攜月遊。

translations.literal: Again next called Four Tubes: north and south as the celestial pivot, in the center a traveling tube that can rise, fall, and rotate; separately a moon path, with 249 crossings arrayed beside to carry the moon's travel.
translations.idiomatic: Again next called Four Tubes: north and south as the celestial pivot, in the center a traveling tube that can rise, fall, and rotate; separately a moon path, with 249 crossings arrayed beside to carry the moon's travel.

sentences.zh: 一行以爲難用，而其法亦亡。

translations.literal: Yixing thought it hard to use, and its method also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing thought it hard to use, and its method also perished.

sentences.zh: 其後率府兵曹梁令瓚更以木爲遊儀，因淳風之法而稍附新意，詔與一行雜校得失，改鑄銅儀，古今稱其詳確。

translations.literal: Afterward Military Affairs Officer Liang Lingzan of the Rate Office further made a traveling instrument of wood, following Chunfeng's method with slight new additions; an edict ordered joint verification with Yixing of gains and losses, and recasting in bronze—the instrument ancient and modern call detailed and exact.

sentences.zh: 至道中，初鑄渾天儀于司天監，多因斛蘭、晁崇之法。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era, the armillary sphere was first cast at the Directorate of Astronomy, largely following Hulu and Chao Chong's methods.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhidao era, the armillary sphere was first cast at the Directorate of Astronomy, largely following Hulu and Chao Chong's methods.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，改鑄銅儀于天文院，姑用令瓚、一行之論，而去取交有失得。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era, the bronze instrument was recast at the Astronomical Observatory, tentatively using Lingzan and Yixing's theories, but in selecting crossings there were gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangyou era, the bronze instrument was recast at the Astronomical Observatory, tentatively using Lingzan and Yixing's theories, but in selecting crossings there were gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 臣今輯古今之說以求數象，有不合者十有三事：

translations.literal: Your subject now compiles ancient and modern theories to seek number and sign—there are thirteen matters that do not accord:
translations.idiomatic: Your subject now compiles ancient and modern theories to seek number and sign—there are thirteen matters that do not accord:

translations.literal: Your subject now compiles ancient and modern theories to seek number and sign—there are thirteen matters that do not accord:
translations.idiomatic: Your subject now compiles ancient and modern theories to seek number and sign—there are thirteen matters that do not accord:

sentences.zh: 其一，舊說以謂今中國于地爲東南，當令西北望極星，置天極不當中北。

translations.literal: First: the old theory holds that present China on earth is southeast; one should look northwest for the pole star, and the celestial pole should not be centered north.
translations.idiomatic: First: the old theory holds that present China on earth is southeast; one should look northwest for the pole star, and the celestial pole should not be centered north.

sentences.zh: 又曰：天常傾西北，極星不得居中。

translations.literal: It also says: heaven constantly tilts northwest, and the pole star cannot be centered.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: heaven constantly tilts northwest, and the pole star cannot be centered.

sentences.zh: 臣謂以中國規觀之，天常北倚可也，謂極星偏西則不然。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that viewing by China's standard, heaven constantly leaning north is acceptable; to say the pole star is shifted west is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that viewing by China's standard, heaven constantly leaning north is acceptable; to say the pole star is shifted west is not so.

sentences.zh: 所謂東西南北者，何從而得之？

translations.literal: What are called east, south, west, and north—how are they obtained?
translations.idiomatic: What are called east, south, west, and north—how are they obtained?

sentences.zh: 豈不以日之所出者爲東，日之所入者爲西乎？

translations.literal: Is it not that where the sun rises is east, and where the sun sets is west?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that where the sun rises is east, and where the sun sets is west?

sentences.zh: 臣觀古之候天者，自安南都護府至浚儀太嶽台才六千里，而北極之差凡十五度，稍北不已，庸詎知極星之不直人上也？

translations.literal: Your subject observes that ancient observers of heaven, from Annam Protectorate to the Great Yue Terrace at Junyi, were only 6,000 li apart, yet the difference in the north pole was 15 degrees in all; going slightly north without end—how can one know the pole star is not directly above people?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes that ancient observers of heaven, from Annam Protectorate to the Great Yue Terrace at Junyi, were only 6,000 li apart, yet the difference in the north pole was 15 degrees in all; going slightly north without end—how can one know the pole star is not directly above people?

sentences.zh: 臣嘗讀黃帝《素書》：「立於午而面子，立於子而面午，至於自卯而望酉，自酉而望卯，皆曰北面。

translations.literal: Your subject once read the Yellow Emperor's Plain Book: 'Standing at wu and facing zi, standing at zi and facing wu; from mao looking at you, from you looking at mao—all are called facing north.'
translations.idiomatic: Your subject once read the Yellow Emperor's Plain Book: 'Standing at wu and facing zi, standing at zi and facing wu; from mao looking at you, from you looking at mao—all are called facing north.'

sentences.zh: 立於卯而負酉，立於酉而負卯，至於自午而望南，自子而望北，則皆曰南面。

translations.literal: 'Standing at mao with you at one's back, standing at you with mao at one's back; from wu looking south, from zi looking north—all are called facing south.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Standing at mao with you at one's back, standing at you with mao at one's back; from wu looking south, from zi looking north—all are called facing south.'

sentences.zh: 」臣始不諭其理，逮今思之，乃常以天中爲北也。

translations.literal: Your subject at first did not understand the principle; reflecting on it now, one always takes heaven's center as north.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject at first did not understand the principle; reflecting on it now, one always takes heaven's center as north.

sentences.zh: 常以天中爲北，則蓋以極星常居天中也。

translations.literal: Always taking heaven's center as north, then the pole star constantly dwells at heaven's center.
translations.idiomatic: Always taking heaven's center as north, then the pole star constantly dwells at heaven's center.

sentences.zh: 《素問》尤爲善言天者。

translations.literal: The Plain Questions especially speaks well of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Plain Questions especially speaks well of heaven.

sentences.zh: 今南北才五百里，則北極輒差一度以上；

translations.literal: Now with only 500 li north and south, the north pole differs by more than one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Now with only 500 li north and south, the north pole differs by more than one degree.

sentences.zh: 而東西南北數千里間，日分之時候之，日未嘗不出於卯半而入於酉半，則又知天樞既中，則日之所出者定爲東，日之所入者定爲西，天樞則常爲北無疑矣。

translations.literal: Yet over several thousand li east, west, south, and north, observing at the time of day-division, the sun never fails to rise at half mao and set at half you—then one further knows that since the celestial pivot is centered, where the sun rises is fixed as east, where it sets is fixed as west, and the celestial pivot is constantly north without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet over several thousand li east, west, south, and north, observing at the time of day-division, the sun never fails to rise at half mao and set at half you—then one further knows that since the celestial pivot is centered, where the sun rises is fixed as east, where it sets is fixed as west, and the celestial pivot is constantly north without doubt.

sentences.zh: 以衡窺之，日分之時，以渾儀抵極星以候日之出沒，則常在卯、酉之半少北。

translations.literal: Observing with the balance tube, at the time of day-division, using the armillary sphere to reach the pole star to observe the sun's rising and setting, it is always at half mao and half you, slightly north.
translations.idiomatic: Observing with the balance tube, at the time of day-division, using the armillary sphere to reach the pole star to observe the sun's rising and setting, it is always at half mao and half you, slightly north.

sentences.zh: 此殆放乎四海而同者，何從而知中國之爲東南也？

translations.literal: This is nearly the same throughout the four seas—how can one know China is southeast?
translations.idiomatic: This is nearly the same throughout the four seas—how can one know China is southeast?

sentences.zh: 彼徒見中國東南皆際海而爲是說也。

translations.literal: They merely saw that China's southeast all borders the sea and made this theory.
translations.idiomatic: They merely saw that China's southeast all borders the sea and made this theory.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂極星之果中、果非中，皆無足論者。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that whether the pole star is truly centered or not is not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that whether the pole star is truly centered or not is not worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 彼北極之出地六千里之間所差者已如是，又安知其茫昧幾千萬里之外邪？

translations.literal: Within the 6,000 li where the north pole rises above earth the difference is already so—how can one know what lies in the dim distance tens of millions of li beyond?
translations.idiomatic: Within the 6,000 li where the north pole rises above earth the difference is already so—how can one know what lies in the dim distance tens of millions of li beyond?

sentences.zh: 今直當據建邦之地，人目之所及者，裁以爲法。

translations.literal: Now one should simply take the land where the state is founded, what the human eye can reach, and cut it as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Now one should simply take the land where the state is founded, what the human eye can reach, and cut it as the standard.

sentences.zh: 不足爲法者，宜置而勿議可也。

translations.literal: What cannot serve as standard should be set aside and not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: What cannot serve as standard should be set aside and not discussed.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：紘平設以象地體，今渾儀置於崇台之上，下瞰日月之所出，則紘不與地際相當者。

translations.literal: Second: the cord level is set to represent the earth's body; now the armillary sphere is placed on a high terrace, looking down on where sun and moon rise—then the cord does not meet the earth's horizon.
translations.idiomatic: Second: the cord level is set to represent the earth's body; now the armillary sphere is placed on a high terrace, looking down on where sun and moon rise—then the cord does not meet the earth's horizon.

sentences.zh: 臣詳此說雖粗有理，然天地之廣大，不爲一台之高下有所推遷。

translations.literal: Your subject examines this theory: though it has rough reason, heaven and earth's vastness is not shifted by a terrace's height or lowness.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject examines this theory: though it has rough reason, heaven and earth's vastness is not shifted by a terrace's height or lowness.

sentences.zh: 蓋渾儀考天地之體，有實數，有准數。

translations.literal: The armillary sphere examines heaven and earth's body—there is actual number and there is proportional number.
translations.idiomatic: The armillary sphere examines heaven and earth's body—there is actual number and there is proportional number.

sentences.zh: 所謂實者，此數即彼數也，此移赤彼亦移赤之謂也。

translations.literal: What is called actual: this number is that number; move this red and that also moves red—such is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: What is called actual: this number is that number; move this red and that also moves red—such is the meaning.

sentences.zh: 所謂准者，以此准彼，此之一分，則准彼之幾千里之謂也。

translations.literal: What is called proportional: use this to proportion that—one fen here proportions to several thousand li there.
translations.idiomatic: What is called proportional: use this to proportion that—one fen here proportions to several thousand li there.

sentences.zh: 今台之高下乃所謂實數，一台之高不過數丈，彼之所差者亦不過此，天地之大，豈數丈足累其高下？

translations.literal: Now the terrace's height or lowness is the so-called actual number; one terrace's height does not exceed several zhang—the difference there also does not exceed this; heaven and earth's greatness—can several zhang suffice to affect their height and lowness?
translations.idiomatic: Now the terrace's height or lowness is the so-called actual number; one terrace's height does not exceed several zhang—the difference there also does not exceed this; heaven and earth's greatness—can several zhang suffice to affect their height and lowness?

sentences.zh: 若衡之低昂，則所謂准數者也。

translations.literal: If the balance's elevation and depression, that is the so-called proportional number.
translations.idiomatic: If the balance's elevation and depression, that is the so-called proportional number.

sentences.zh: 衡移一分，則彼不知其數幾千里，則衡之低昂當審，而台之高下非所當恤也。

translations.literal: The balance moves one fen, and there one does not know the number of several thousand li—therefore the balance's elevation and depression should be examined carefully, while the terrace's height and lowness is not what should concern one.
translations.idiomatic: The balance moves one fen, and there one does not know the number of several thousand li—therefore the balance's elevation and depression should be examined carefully, while the terrace's height and lowness is not what should concern one.

translations.literal: Second: the cord level is set to represent the earth's body; now the armillary sphere is placed on a high terrace, looking down on where sun and moon rise—then the cord does not meet the earth's horizon. Your subject examines this theory: though it has rough reason, heaven and earth's vastness is not shifted by a terrace's height or lowness. The armillary sphere examines heaven and earth's body—there is actual number and there is proportional number. What is called actual: this number is that number; move this red and that also moves red—such is the meaning. What is called proportional: use this to proportion that—one fen here proportions to several thousand li there. Now the terrace's height or lowness is the so-called actual number; one terrace's height does not exceed several zhang—the difference there also does not exceed this; heaven and earth's greatness—can several zhang suffice to affect their height and lowness? If the balance's elevation and depression, that is the so-called proportional number. The balance moves one fen, and there one does not know the number of several thousand li—therefore the balance's elevation and depression should be examined carefully, while the terrace's height and lowness is not what should concern one.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：月行之道，過交則入黃道六度而稍卻，復交則出於黃道之南，亦如之。

translations.literal: Third: the moon's path—passing the crossing it enters the ecliptic six degrees and slightly retreats; crossing again it exits south of the ecliptic, likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the moon's path—passing the crossing it enters the ecliptic six degrees and slightly retreats; crossing again it exits south of the ecliptic, likewise.

sentences.zh: 月行周于黃道，如繩之繞木，故月交而行日之陰，則日爲之虧；

translations.literal: The moon travels circling the ecliptic like a cord winding a post; therefore when the moon crosses and travels on the sun's yin side, the sun is eclipsed for it.
translations.idiomatic: The moon travels circling the ecliptic like a cord winding a post; therefore when the moon crosses and travels on the sun's yin side, the sun is eclipsed for it.

sentences.zh: 入蝕法而不虧者，行日之陽也。

translations.literal: Entering the eclipse method yet not eclipsed—traveling on the sun's yang side.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the eclipse method yet not eclipsed—traveling on the sun's yang side.

sentences.zh: 每月退交二百四十九周有奇，然後復會。

translations.literal: Each month it retreats one crossing, 249 circuits and a fraction, then meets again.
translations.idiomatic: Each month it retreats one crossing, 249 circuits and a fraction, then meets again.

sentences.zh: 今月道既不能環繞黃道，又退交之漸當每日差池，今必候月終而頓移，亦終不能符會天度，當省去月環。

translations.literal: Now the moon path cannot encircle the ecliptic, and the gradual retreat of crossings should differ daily; now one must wait until month's end to shift suddenly—still it cannot match heavenly degrees; the moon ring should be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Now the moon path cannot encircle the ecliptic, and the gradual retreat of crossings should differ daily; now one must wait until month's end to shift suddenly—still it cannot match heavenly degrees; the moon ring should be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 其候月之出入，專以曆法步之。

translations.literal: Observing the moon's entering and exiting should rely solely on calendar method to step it.
translations.idiomatic: Observing the moon's entering and exiting should rely solely on calendar method to step it.

sentences.zh: 其四，衡上、下二端皆徑一度有半，用日之徑也。

translations.literal: Fourth: the balance's upper and lower two ends are each one and a half degrees in diameter, using the sun's diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: the balance's upper and lower two ends are each one and a half degrees in diameter, using the sun's diameter.

sentences.zh: 若衡端不能全容日月之體，則無由審日月定次。

translations.literal: If the balance end cannot fully contain the sun and moon's bodies, there is no means to examine the sun and moon's fixed positions.
translations.idiomatic: If the balance end cannot fully contain the sun and moon's bodies, there is no means to examine the sun and moon's fixed positions.

sentences.zh: 欲日月正滿上衡之端，不可動移，此其所以用一度有半爲法也。

translations.literal: Wishing the sun and moon to fill exactly the upper balance end, immovable—this is why one and a half degrees is used as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing the sun and moon to fill exactly the upper balance end, immovable—this is why one and a half degrees is used as the standard.

sentences.zh: 下端亦一度有半，則不然。

translations.literal: The lower end also one and a half degrees—this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: The lower end also one and a half degrees—this is not so.

sentences.zh: 若人目迫下端之東以窺上端之西，則差幾三度。

translations.literal: If the human eye presses the lower end's east to peep at the upper end's west, the difference is nearly three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: If the human eye presses the lower end's east to peep at the upper end's west, the difference is nearly three degrees.

sentences.zh: 凡求星之法，必令所求之星正當穿之中心。

translations.literal: For all methods of seeking stars, one must make the sought star exactly at the piercing's center.
translations.idiomatic: For all methods of seeking stars, one must make the sought star exactly at the piercing's center.

sentences.zh: 今兩端既等，則人目遊動，無因知其正中。

translations.literal: Now both ends being equal, the human eye moves—there is no means to know the exact center.
translations.idiomatic: Now both ends being equal, the human eye moves—there is no means to know the exact center.

sentences.zh: 今以鉤股法求之，下徑三分，上徑一度有半，則兩竅相覆，大小略等。

translations.literal: Now using gougu method to seek it: lower diameter three fen, upper diameter one and a half degrees—then the two apertures overlap, sizes roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Now using gougu method to seek it: lower diameter three fen, upper diameter one and a half degrees—then the two apertures overlap, sizes roughly equal.

sentences.zh: 人目不搖，則所察自正。

translations.literal: The human eye not swaying, what is observed is naturally correct.
translations.idiomatic: The human eye not swaying, what is observed is naturally correct.

sentences.zh: 其五，前世皆以極星爲天中，自祖暅以璣衡窺考天極不動處，乃在極星之末猶一度有餘。

translations.literal: Fifth: former ages all took the pole star as heaven's center; from Zu Geng using the armillary sphere to observe and examine, the unmoving place of the celestial pole is still more than one degree beyond the pole star's tip.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: former ages all took the pole star as heaven's center; from Zu Geng using the armillary sphere to observe and examine, the unmoving place of the celestial pole is still more than one degree beyond the pole star's tip.

sentences.zh: 今銅儀天樞內徑一度有半，乃謬以衡端之度爲率。

translations.literal: Now the bronze instrument's celestial pivot inner diameter is one and a half degrees—mistakenly taking the balance end's degree as the rate.
translations.idiomatic: Now the bronze instrument's celestial pivot inner diameter is one and a half degrees—mistakenly taking the balance end's degree as the rate.

sentences.zh: 若璣衡端平，則極星常遊天樞之外；

translations.literal: If the armillary sphere end is level, the pole star constantly travels outside the celestial pivot.
translations.idiomatic: If the armillary sphere end is level, the pole star constantly travels outside the celestial pivot.

sentences.zh: 璣衡小偏，則極星乍出乍入。

translations.literal: If the armillary sphere is slightly off-center, the pole star now exits now enters.
translations.idiomatic: If the armillary sphere is slightly off-center, the pole star now exits now enters.

sentences.zh: 令瓚舊法，天樞乃徑二度有半，蓋欲使極星游於樞中也。

translations.literal: Lingzan's old method: the celestial pivot diameter was two and a half degrees—intending to make the pole star travel within the pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzan's old method: the celestial pivot diameter was two and a half degrees—intending to make the pole star travel within the pivot.

sentences.zh: 臣考驗極星更三月，而後知天中不動處遠極星乃三度有餘，則祖暅窺考猶爲未審。

translations.literal: Your subject examined the pole star through three months, then knew the unmoving place of heaven's center is more than three degrees from the pole star—then Zu Geng's observation was still not exact.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject examined the pole star through three months, then knew the unmoving place of heaven's center is more than three degrees from the pole star—then Zu Geng's observation was still not exact.

sentences.zh: 今當爲天樞徑七度，使人目切南樞望之，星正循北極樞裏周常見不隱，天體方正。

translations.literal: Now the celestial pivot should be seven degrees in diameter, making the human eye press against the south pivot to look—the star circulates within the north polar pivot, constantly visible and not hidden, the celestial body square and correct.

sentences.zh: 其六，令瓚以辰刻、十幹、八卦皆刻於紘，然紘平正而黃道斜運，當子、午之間，則日徑度而道促；

translations.literal: Sixth: Lingzan carved double-hours, ten stems, and Eight Trigrams all on the cord; yet the cord is level and correct while the ecliptic travels obliquely—between zi and wu the sun's diameter is compressed and the path short.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: Lingzan carved double-hours, ten stems, and Eight Trigrams all on the cord; yet the cord is level and correct while the ecliptic travels obliquely—between zi and wu the sun's diameter is compressed and the path short.

sentences.zh: 卯、酉之際，則日迤行而道舒。

translations.literal: At mao and you the sun travels winding and the path slack.
translations.idiomatic: At mao and you the sun travels winding and the path slack.

sentences.zh: 如此，辰刻不能無謬。

translations.literal: Thus double-hours cannot be without error.
translations.idiomatic: Thus double-hours cannot be without error.

sentences.zh: 新銅儀則移刻於緯，四游均平，辰刻不失。

translations.literal: The new bronze instrument then moves the quarters to the latitude ring; the four tubes are evenly level, double-hours without loss.
translations.idiomatic: The new bronze instrument then moves the quarters to the latitude ring; the four tubes are evenly level, double-hours without loss.

sentences.zh: 然令瓚天中單環，直中國人頂之上，而新銅儀緯斜絡南北極之中，與赤道相直。

translations.literal: Yet Lingzan's heaven-center single ring stood directly above the heads of people in China, while the new bronze instrument's latitude ring slants across between north and south poles, perpendicular to the equator.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lingzan's heaven-center single ring stood directly above the heads of people in China, while the new bronze instrument's latitude ring slants across between north and south poles, perpendicular to the equator.

sentences.zh: 舊法設之無用，新儀移之爲是。

translations.literal: The old method's setting was useless; the new instrument's moving it is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The old method's setting was useless; the new instrument's moving it is correct.

sentences.zh: 然當側窺如車輪之牙，而不當衡規如鼓陶，其旁迫狹，難賦辰刻，而又蔽映星度。

translations.literal: Yet one should observe sidelong like a wheel's teeth, not like a balance ring like a drum pot—its sides cramped and narrow, hard to assign double-hours, and also obscuring stellar degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one should observe sidelong like a wheel's teeth, not like a balance ring like a drum pot—its sides cramped and narrow, hard to assign double-hours, and also obscuring stellar degrees.

sentences.zh: 其七，司天銅儀，黃、赤道與紘合鑄，不可轉移，雖與天運不符，至於窺測之時，先以距度星考定三辰所舍，復運遊儀抵本宿度，乃求出入黃道與去極度，所得無以異於令瓚之術。

translations.literal: Seventh: the Directorate's bronze instrument—yellow and red equators and cord cast together, immovable; though not matching heaven's motion, at the time of observation, first use distance-degree stars to examine and fix where the three luminaries lodge, then turn the traveling instrument to reach the original lodge degree, then seek entering and exiting the ecliptic and distance from the pole—the results differ not from Lingzan's method.

sentences.zh: 其法本于晁崇、斛蘭之舊制，雖不甚精縟，而頗爲簡易。

translations.literal: The method originally derives from Chao Chong and Hulu's old construction—though not very refined, it is quite simple.
translations.idiomatic: The method originally derives from Chao Chong and Hulu's old construction—though not very refined, it is quite simple.

sentences.zh: 李淳風嘗謂斛蘭所作鐵儀，赤道不動，乃如膠柱。

translations.literal: Li Chunfeng once said Hulu's iron instrument, the equator unmoving, was like gluing the pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng once said Hulu's iron instrument, the equator unmoving, was like gluing the pillar.

sentences.zh: 以考月行，差或至十七度，少不減十度。

translations.literal: Examining the moon's motion, the error could reach 17 degrees, at least not less than 10 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the moon's motion, the error could reach 17 degrees, at least not less than 10 degrees.

sentences.zh: 此正謂直以赤道候月行，其差如此。

translations.literal: This precisely means directly using the equator to observe the moon's motion—the error was thus.
translations.idiomatic: This precisely means directly using the equator to observe the moon's motion—the error was thus.

sentences.zh: 今黃、赤道度，再運遊儀抵所舍宿度求之，而月行則以月曆每日去極度算率之，不可謂之膠也。

translations.literal: Now yellow and red equator degrees, again turning the traveling instrument to reach the lodged lodge degree to seek them; moon motion is then calculated by daily distance-from-pole rate from the lunar calendar—this cannot be called glued.

sentences.zh: 其八，令瓚舊法，黃道設於月道之上，赤道又次月道，而璣最處其下。

translations.literal: Eighth: Lingzan's old method set the ecliptic above the moon path, the equator again below the moon path, and ji lowest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: Lingzan's old method set the ecliptic above the moon path, the equator again below the moon path, and ji lowest of all.

sentences.zh: 每月移一交，則黃、赤道輒變。

translations.literal: Each month moving one crossing, yellow and red equators then changed.
translations.idiomatic: Each month moving one crossing, yellow and red equators then changed.

sentences.zh: 今當省去月道，徙璣於赤道之上，而黃道居赤道之下，則二道與衡端相迫，而星度易審。

translations.literal: Now the moon path should be eliminated, ji moved above the equator, and the ecliptic placed below the equator—then the two paths press close to the balance end, and stellar degrees are easy to examine.
translations.idiomatic: Now the moon path should be eliminated, ji moved above the equator, and the ecliptic placed below the equator—then the two paths press close to the balance end, and stellar degrees are easy to examine.

sentences.zh: 其九，舊法：規環一面刻周天度，一面加銀丁。

translations.literal: Ninth, old method: the ring's one face carved the full circuit degrees, one face added silver studs.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, old method: the ring's one face carved the full circuit degrees, one face added silver studs.

sentences.zh: 所以施銀丁者，夜候天晦，不可目察，則以手切之也。

translations.literal: The reason for applying silver studs: observing heaven at night when dark, unable to see with the eye, one cuts with the hand.
translations.idiomatic: The reason for applying silver studs: observing heaven at night when dark, unable to see with the eye, one cuts with the hand.

sentences.zh: 古之人以璿爲之，璿者，珠之屬也。

translations.literal: Ancient people used xuan for this—xuan is a kind of pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient people used xuan for this—xuan is a kind of pearl.

sentences.zh: 今司天監三辰儀設齒於環背，不與橫蕭會，當移列兩旁，以便參察。

sentences.zh: 其十，舊法：重璣皆廣四寸，厚四分。

translations.literal: Tenth, old method: heavy ji all four cun wide, four fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, old method: heavy ji all four cun wide, four fen thick.

sentences.zh: 其他規軸，椎重樸拙，不可旋運。

translations.literal: Other rings and axles were heavy, crude, and unable to rotate.
translations.idiomatic: Other rings and axles were heavy, crude, and unable to rotate.

sentences.zh: 今小損其制，使之輕利。

translations.literal: Now slightly reduce the construction, making it light and nimble.
translations.idiomatic: Now slightly reduce the construction, making it light and nimble.

sentences.zh: 其十一，古之人知黃道歲易，不知赤道之因變也。

translations.literal: Eleventh: ancient people knew the ecliptic shifts yearly, but did not know the equator shifts accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh: ancient people knew the ecliptic shifts yearly, but did not know the equator shifts accordingly.

sentences.zh: 黃道之度，與赤道之度相偶者也。

translations.literal: Ecliptic degrees and equatorial degrees are paired.
translations.idiomatic: Ecliptic degrees and equatorial degrees are paired.

sentences.zh: 黃道徙而西，則赤道不得獨膠。

translations.literal: When the ecliptic shifts west, the equator cannot alone remain glued.
translations.idiomatic: When the ecliptic shifts west, the equator cannot alone remain glued.

sentences.zh: 今當變赤道與黃道同法。

translations.literal: Now the equator should be changed to the same method as the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Now the equator should be changed to the same method as the ecliptic.

translations.literal: Twelfth, old method: yellow and red equators set level, directly blocking stellar degrees, obscuring the human eye, unable to observe.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, old method: yellow and red equators set level, directly blocking stellar degrees, obscuring the human eye, unable to observe.

sentences.zh: 其後乃別加鑽孔，尤爲拙謬。

translations.literal: Afterward they separately added drilled holes—especially crude and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they separately added drilled holes—especially crude and absurd.

sentences.zh: 今當側置少偏，使天度出北際之外，自不淩蔽。

translations.literal: Now they should be set sidelong, slightly off-center, making stellar degrees emerge beyond the north edge, naturally not obscured.
translations.idiomatic: Now they should be set sidelong, slightly off-center, making stellar degrees emerge beyond the north edge, naturally not obscured.

translations.literal: Thirteenth, old method: the earth cord vertically crossed half the celestial meridian; for all observing the three luminaries' rising and setting, the earth horizon was exactly covered by the earth cord.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth, old method: the earth cord vertically crossed half the celestial meridian; for all observing the three luminaries' rising and setting, the earth horizon was exactly covered by the earth cord.

sentences.zh: 今當徙紘稍下，使地際與紘之上際相直。

translations.literal: Now the cord should be moved slightly down, making the earth horizon align with the cord's upper edge.
translations.idiomatic: Now the cord should be moved slightly down, making the earth horizon align with the cord's upper edge.

sentences.zh: 候三辰伏見，專以紘際爲率，自當默與天合。

translations.literal: Observing the three luminaries' hiding and visibility, relying solely on the cord edge as rate—it should silently accord with heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Observing the three luminaries' hiding and visibility, relying solely on the cord edge as rate—it should silently accord with heaven.

translations.idiomatic: The armillary sphere as instrument has three parts, mutually dependent in use.

sentences.zh: 其在外者曰體，以立四方上下之定位。

translations.literal: The outermost is called the body, to establish the fixed positions of the four directions, above and below.
translations.idiomatic: The outermost is called the body, to establish the fixed positions of the four directions, above and below.

sentences.zh: 其次曰象，以法天之運行，常與天隨。

translations.literal: Next is called the image, to model heaven's motion, constantly following heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Next is called the image, to model heaven's motion, constantly following heaven.

sentences.zh: 其在內璣衡，璣以察緯，衡以察經。

translations.literal: Within are ji and heng—ji to examine latitude, heng to examine longitude.
translations.idiomatic: Within are ji and heng—ji to examine latitude, heng to examine longitude.

sentences.zh: 求天地端極三明匿見者，體爲之用；

translations.literal: Seeking heaven and earth's endpoints and the three luminaries' hiding and visibility—the body serves.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking heaven and earth's endpoints and the three luminaries' hiding and visibility—the body serves.

sentences.zh: 察黃道降陟辰刻運徙者，象爲之用；

translations.literal: Examining the ecliptic's rise and fall, double-hours, and motion and shift—the image serves.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the ecliptic's rise and fall, double-hours, and motion and shift—the image serves.

sentences.zh: 四方上下無所不屬者，璣衡爲之用。

translations.literal: The four directions, above and below, nothing not belonging to—ji and heng serve.
translations.idiomatic: The four directions, above and below, nothing not belonging to—ji and heng serve.

sentences.zh: 體之爲器，爲圓規者四。

translations.literal: The body as instrument has four circular rings.
translations.idiomatic: The body as instrument has four circular rings.

sentences.zh: 其規之別：一曰經，經之規二並峙，正抵子午，若車輪之植。

translations.literal: The ring types: first called meridian—two meridian rings stand together, directly reaching zi and wu, like a wheel planted upright.
translations.idiomatic: The ring types: first called meridian—two meridian rings stand together, directly reaching zi and wu, like a wheel planted upright.

sentences.zh: 二規相距四寸，夾規爲齒，以別去極之度。

translations.literal: The two rings four cun apart, teeth between the rings to distinguish degrees from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: The two rings four cun apart, teeth between the rings to distinguish degrees from the pole.

sentences.zh: 北極出紘之上三十有四度十分度之八強，南極下紘亦如之。

translations.literal: The north pole rises 34 degrees and eight-tenths of a degree above the cord; the south pole descends below the cord likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The north pole rises 34 degrees and eight-tenths of a degree above the cord; the south pole descends below the cord likewise.

sentences.zh: 對銜二釭，聯二規以爲一，釭中容樞。

translations.literal: Two pins face each other, linking the two rings as one; the pin holds the pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Two pins face each other, linking the two rings as one; the pin holds the pivot.

sentences.zh: 二曰緯，緯之規一，與經交於二極之中，若車輪之倚，南北距極皆九十一度強。

translations.literal: Second called latitude—one latitude ring, crossing the meridian at the two poles' center, like a wheel leaning; north and south each 91-odd degrees from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Second called latitude—one latitude ring, crossing the meridian at the two poles' center, like a wheel leaning; north and south each 91-odd degrees from the pole.

sentences.zh: 夾規爲齒，以別周天之度。

translations.literal: Teeth between the ring to distinguish the full circuit degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Teeth between the ring to distinguish the full circuit degrees.

sentences.zh: 三曰紘，紘之規一，上際當經之半，若車輪之僕，以考地際，周賦十二辰，以定八方。

translations.literal: Third called cord—one cord ring, upper edge at half the meridian, like a wheel prostrate, to examine the earth horizon; the twelve branches assigned around to fix the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Third called cord—one cord ring, upper edge at half the meridian, like a wheel prostrate, to examine the earth horizon; the twelve branches assigned around to fix the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 紘之下有趺，從一衡一，刻溝受水以爲平。

translations.literal: Below the cord is a base, following one crossbeam, channels carved to receive water as level.
translations.idiomatic: Below the cord is a base, following one crossbeam, channels carved to receive water as level.

sentences.zh: 中溝爲地，以受注水。

translations.literal: The center channel is earth, to receive poured water.
translations.idiomatic: The center channel is earth, to receive poured water.

sentences.zh: 四末建趺，爲升龍四以負紘。

translations.literal: At the four corners bases are built, four ascending dragons to bear the cord.
translations.idiomatic: At the four corners bases are built, four ascending dragons to bear the cord.

sentences.zh: 凡渾儀之屬皆屬焉。

translations.literal: All parts of the armillary sphere belong to these.
translations.idiomatic: All parts of the armillary sphere belong to these.

translations.idiomatic: The dragon throats are the four anchors of the net to make it firm.

translations.literal: Second called equator—one equator ring, ji three-tenths of a cun to hold the equator.
translations.idiomatic: Second called equator—one equator ring, ji three-tenths of a cun to hold the equator.

sentences.zh: 赤道設之如緯，其異者緯膠於經，而赤道銜於璣，有時而移，度穿一竅，以移歲差。

translations.literal: The equator set like latitude; the difference: latitude is glued to the meridian, while the equator is held by ji, moving at times; degrees pierce one hole to shift precession.
translations.idiomatic: The equator set like latitude; the difference: latitude is glued to the meridian, while the equator is held by ji, moving at times; degrees pierce one hole to shift precession.

translations.idiomatic: Crossing at Straddle and Horn, degrees pierce one hole, bound to the equator with copper wire.

sentences.zh: 歲差盈度，則並赤道徙而西。

translations.idiomatic: When precession exceeds degrees, the equator shifts west together.

translations.idiomatic: Yellow and red equator teeth between rings to distinguish equal and winding degrees.
