Heng can rise and fall, to examine omens above and below.

sentences.zh: 《浮漏議》曰：

translations.literal: The Memorial on the Clepsydra says:
translations.idiomatic: The Memorial on the Clepsydra says:

translations.literal: The Memorial on the Clepsydra says:
translations.idiomatic: The Memorial on the Clepsydra says:

sentences.zh: 播水之壺三，而受水之壺一。

translations.literal: Three vessels that broadcast water, and one vessel that receives water.
translations.idiomatic: Three vessels that broadcast water, and one vessel that receives water.

sentences.zh: 曰求壺、廢壺，方中皆圓尺有八寸，尺有四寸五分以深，其食二斛，爲積分四百六十六萬六千四百六十。

translations.literal: Called the seeking vessel and waste vessel: square within, circular one chi eight cun, one chi four cun five fen deep; capacity two hu, volume 4,666,460 fen.
translations.idiomatic: Called the seeking vessel and waste vessel: square within, circular one chi eight cun, one chi four cun five fen deep; capacity two hu, volume 4,666,460 fen.

sentences.zh: 曰復壺，如求壺之度，中離以爲二，元一斛介八斗，而中有達。

translations.literal: Called the recovery vessel: like the seeking vessel's measure, divided in the center into two, originally one hu plus eight dou, with a passage within.
translations.idiomatic: Called the recovery vessel: like the seeking vessel's measure, divided in the center into two, originally one hu plus eight dou, with a passage within.

sentences.zh: 曰建壺，方尺植三尺有五寸，其食斛有半。

translations.literal: Called the building vessel: square one chi, upright three chi five cun, capacity one and a half hu.
translations.idiomatic: Called the building vessel: square one chi, upright three chi five cun, capacity one and a half hu.

sentences.zh: 求壺之水，復壺之所求也。

translations.literal: The seeking vessel's water is what the recovery vessel seeks.
translations.idiomatic: The seeking vessel's water is what the recovery vessel seeks.

sentences.zh: 壺盈則水馳，壺虛則水凝。

translations.literal: When the vessel is full water runs swiftly; when empty water congeals.
translations.idiomatic: When the vessel is full water runs swiftly; when empty water congeals.

sentences.zh: 復壺之肋爲枝渠，以爲水節。

translations.literal: The recovery vessel's ribs are branch channels, serving as water regulators.
translations.idiomatic: The recovery vessel's ribs are branch channels, serving as water regulators.

sentences.zh: 求壺進水暴，則流怒以搖，復以壺，又折以爲介。

translations.literal: When the seeking vessel's inflow is violent, the flow rages and shakes; again using the recovery vessel, again bent as a divider.
translations.idiomatic: When the seeking vessel's inflow is violent, the flow rages and shakes; again using the recovery vessel, again bent as a divider.

sentences.zh: 復爲枝渠，達其濫溢。

translations.literal: Again branch channels made, reaching its overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Again branch channels made, reaching its overflow.

sentences.zh: 枝渠之委，所謂廢壺也，以受廢水。

translations.literal: The branch channel's discharge—the so-called waste vessel—receives waste water.
translations.idiomatic: The branch channel's discharge—the so-called waste vessel—receives waste water.

sentences.zh: 三壺皆所以播水，爲水制也。

translations.literal: All three vessels broadcast water, forming the water system.
translations.idiomatic: All three vessels broadcast water, forming the water system.

sentences.zh: 自復壺之介，以玉權釃於建壺，建壺所以受水爲刻者也。

translations.literal: From the recovery vessel's divider, jade weights pour into the building vessel—the building vessel receives water to mark quarters.
translations.idiomatic: From the recovery vessel's divider, jade weights pour into the building vessel—the building vessel receives water to mark quarters.

sentences.zh: 建壺一易箭，則發上室以瀉之。

translations.literal: When the building vessel changes one arrow, the upper chamber is opened to drain it.
translations.idiomatic: When the building vessel changes one arrow, the upper chamber is opened to drain it.

sentences.zh: 求、復、建壺之泄，皆欲迫下，水所趣也。

translations.literal: The seeking, recovery, and building vessels' outflow—all wish to press downward, where water tends.
translations.idiomatic: The seeking, recovery, and building vessels' outflow—all wish to press downward, where water tends.

sentences.zh: 玉權下水之概寸，矯而上之然後發，則水撓而不躁也。

translations.literal: The jade weight's lower water gate one cun, bent upward then released—then water flows gently without turbulence.
translations.idiomatic: The jade weight's lower water gate one cun, bent upward then released—then water flows gently without turbulence.

sentences.zh: 復壺之達半求壺之注，玉權半復壺之達。

translations.literal: The recovery vessel's passage half the seeking vessel's pour; the jade weight half the recovery vessel's passage.
translations.idiomatic: The recovery vessel's passage half the seeking vessel's pour; the jade weight half the recovery vessel's passage.

sentences.zh: 枝渠博皆分，高如其博，平方如砥，以爲水概。

translations.literal: Branch channel width all one fen, height like its width, square and flat like a whetstone, serving as water gate.
translations.idiomatic: Branch channel width all one fen, height like its width, square and flat like a whetstone, serving as water gate.

sentences.zh: 壺皆爲之冪，無使穢遊，則水道不慧。

translations.literal: All vessels have covers, not letting filth float—then the waterway is not obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: All vessels have covers, not letting filth float—then the waterway is not obstructed.

sentences.zh: 求壺之冪龍紐，以其出水不窮也。

translations.literal: The seeking vessel's cover has a dragon knob, because its outflow is inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: The seeking vessel's cover has a dragon knob, because its outflow is inexhaustible.

sentences.zh: 復壺士紐，士所以生法者，復壺制法之器也。

translations.literal: The recovery vessel has an earth knob—earth is what generates law; the recovery vessel is the instrument that generates law.
translations.idiomatic: The recovery vessel has an earth knob—earth is what generates law; the recovery vessel is the instrument that generates law.

sentences.zh: 廢壺鯢紐，止水之沈，鯢所伏也。

translations.literal: The waste vessel has a salamander knob—salamander is what sinks in still water, where the salamander hides.
translations.idiomatic: The waste vessel has a salamander knob—salamander is what sinks in still water, where the salamander hides.

sentences.zh: 銅史令刻，執漏政也。

translations.literal: The bronze clerk marks quarters, holding the clepsydra's governance.
translations.idiomatic: The bronze clerk marks quarters, holding the clepsydra's governance.

sentences.zh: 冬設煴燎，以澤凝也。

translations.literal: In winter warming fires are set, to moisten congelation.
translations.idiomatic: In winter warming fires are set, to moisten congelation.

sentences.zh: 注水以龍噣直頸附於壺體，直則易浚，附於壺體則難敗。

translations.literal: Water is poured through a dragon mouth with straight neck attached to the vessel body—straight then easy to dredge, attached to the body then hard to break.
translations.idiomatic: Water is poured through a dragon mouth with straight neck attached to the vessel body—straight then easy to dredge, attached to the body then hard to break.

sentences.zh: 復壺玉爲之喙，銜于龍噣，謂之權，所以權其盈虛也。

translations.literal: The recovery vessel's jade beak, held in the dragon mouth, called the weight—thus to weigh its fullness and emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: The recovery vessel's jade beak, held in the dragon mouth, called the weight—thus to weigh its fullness and emptiness.

sentences.zh: 建壺之執窒瓬塗而彌之以重帛，窒則不吐也。

translations.literal: The building vessel's hold is sealed with tile-coating and covered with heavy cloth—sealed then it does not spurt.
translations.idiomatic: The building vessel's hold is sealed with tile-coating and covered with heavy cloth—sealed then it does not spurt.

sentences.zh: 管之善利者，水所溲也，非玉則不能堅良以久。

translations.literal: Of tubes, the good and sharp are what water erodes—without jade they cannot be firm and fine for long.
translations.idiomatic: Of tubes, the good and sharp are what water erodes—without jade they cannot be firm and fine for long.

sentences.zh: 權之所出高則源輕，源輕則其委不悍而溲物不利。

translations.literal: Where the weight emerges high, the source is light; source light then its discharge is not fierce and erodes objects unfavorably.
translations.idiomatic: Where the weight emerges high, the source is light; source light then its discharge is not fierce and erodes objects unfavorably.

sentences.zh: 箭不效於璣衡，則易權、洗箭而改畫，覆以璣衡，謂之常不弊之術。

translations.literal: If the arrow does not match the armillary sphere, change the weight, wash the arrow and alter the marks, cover with the armillary sphere—called the method of constant non-decay.
translations.idiomatic: If the arrow does not match the armillary sphere, change the weight, wash the arrow and alter the marks, cover with the armillary sphere—called the method of constant non-decay.

sentences.zh: 今之下漏者，始嘗甚密，久復先大者管泐也。

translations.literal: Present clepsydrae at first are very precise; after long time again the large tube erodes first.
translations.idiomatic: Present clepsydrae at first are very precise; after long time again the large tube erodes first.

sentences.zh: 管泐而器皆弊者，無權也。

translations.literal: Tube eroded and all vessels decayed—no weight.
translations.idiomatic: Tube eroded and all vessels decayed—no weight.

sentences.zh: 弊而不可復壽者，術固也。

translations.literal: Decayed and unable to restore life—the method is fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Decayed and unable to restore life—the method is fixed.

sentences.zh: 察日之晷以璣衡，而制箭以日之晷跡，一刻之度，以賦餘刻，刻有不均者，建壺有眚也。

translations.literal: Examining the sun's shadow with the armillary sphere, and making the arrow from the sun's shadow trace—one quarter's degree, to assign the remaining quarters; quarters uneven—the building vessel has fault.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the sun's shadow with the armillary sphere, and making the arrow from the sun's shadow trace—one quarter's degree, to assign the remaining quarters; quarters uneven—the building vessel has fault.

sentences.zh: 贅者磨之，創者補之，百刻一度，其壺乃善。

translations.literal: Superfluous parts grind them; damaged parts repair them—one hundred quarters one degree, then the vessel is good.
translations.idiomatic: Superfluous parts grind them; damaged parts repair them—one hundred quarters one degree, then the vessel is good.

sentences.zh: 晝夜已復，而箭有餘才者，權鄙也。

translations.literal: Day and night already completed yet the arrow has surplus—weight is coarse.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night already completed yet the arrow has surplus—weight is coarse.

sentences.zh: 晝夜未復，而壺吐者，權沃也。

translations.literal: Day and night not yet completed yet the vessel spouts—weight is saturated.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night not yet completed yet the vessel spouts—weight is saturated.

sentences.zh: 如是，則調其權，此制器之法也。

translations.literal: Thus adjust the weight—this is the method of constructing the instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Thus adjust the weight—this is the method of constructing the instrument.

sentences.zh: 下漏必用甘泉，惡其垽之爲壺眚也。

translations.literal: Clepsydrae must use sweet spring, hating that sediment becomes vessel fault.
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydrae must use sweet spring, hating that sediment becomes vessel fault.

sentences.zh: 必用一源泉之冽者，權之而重，重則敏於行，而爲箭之情慓；

translations.literal: Must use one spring source that is pure; weigh it and it is heavy—heavy then swift in motion, and the arrow's nature is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Must use one spring source that is pure; weigh it and it is heavy—heavy then swift in motion, and the arrow's nature is urgent.

sentences.zh: 泉之鹵者，權之而輕，輕則椎於行，而爲箭之情駑。

translations.literal: Brackish spring, weigh it and it is light—light then sluggish in motion, and the arrow's nature is slow.
translations.idiomatic: Brackish spring, weigh it and it is light—light then sluggish in motion, and the arrow's nature is slow.

sentences.zh: 一井不可他汲，數汲則泉濁。

translations.literal: One well cannot be drawn from elsewhere; repeated drawing and the spring becomes turbid.
translations.idiomatic: One well cannot be drawn from elsewhere; repeated drawing and the spring becomes turbid.

sentences.zh: 陳水不可再注，再注則行利。

translations.literal: Stale water cannot be poured again; poured again then motion is sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Stale water cannot be poured again; poured again then motion is sharp.

sentences.zh: 此下漏之法也。

translations.literal: This is the method of the clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: This is the method of the clepsydra.

Must use one spring source that is pure; weigh it and it is heavy—heavy then swift in motion, and the arrow's nature is urgent. Brackish spring, weigh it and it is light—light then sluggish in motion, and the arrow's nature is slow. One well cannot be drawn from elsewhere; repeated drawing and the spring becomes turbid. Stale water cannot be poured again; poured again then motion is sharp. This is the method of the clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 箭一如建壺之長，廣寸有五分，三分去二以爲之厚，其陽爲百刻，爲十二辰。

translations.literal: The arrow like the building vessel's length, one cun five fen wide, two-thirds of three fen taken as thickness; the yang side has hundred quarters, twelve branches.
translations.idiomatic: The arrow like the building vessel's length, one cun five fen wide, two-thirds of three fen taken as thickness; the yang side has hundred quarters, twelve branches.

sentences.zh: 博牘二十有一，如箭之長，廣五分，去半以爲之厚。

translations.literal: Broad tablets twenty-one, like the arrow's length, five fen wide, half taken as thickness.
translations.idiomatic: Broad tablets twenty-one, like the arrow's length, five fen wide, half taken as thickness.

sentences.zh: 陽爲五更，爲二十有五籌；

translations.literal: Yang side five watches, twenty-five tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Yang side five watches, twenty-five tallies.

sentences.zh: 陰刻消長之衰。

translations.literal: Yin side carved with waxing and waning decline.
translations.idiomatic: Yin side carved with waxing and waning decline.

sentences.zh: 三分箭之廣，其中刻契以容牘。

translations.literal: One-third the arrow's width, within carved notches to hold tablets.
translations.idiomatic: One-third the arrow's width, within carved notches to hold tablets.

sentences.zh: 夜算差一刻，則因箭而易牘。

translations.literal: Night calculation differs one quarter, then change tablets according to the arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Night calculation differs one quarter, then change tablets according to the arrow.

sentences.zh: 鐐匏，箭舟也。

translations.literal: The chain gourd is the arrow boat.
translations.idiomatic: The chain gourd is the arrow boat.

sentences.zh: 其虛五升，重一鎰有半。

translations.literal: Its empty capacity five sheng, weight one yi and a half.
translations.idiomatic: Its empty capacity five sheng, weight one yi and a half.

sentences.zh: 鍛而赤柔者金之美者也，然後漬而不墨，墨者其久必蝕。

translations.literal: Forged red and soft is the beauty of metal; then steeped and not black—black then in time it must corrode.
translations.idiomatic: Forged red and soft is the beauty of metal; then steeped and not black—black then in time it must corrode.

sentences.zh: 銀之有銅則墨，銅之有錫則屑，特銅久灂則腹敗而飲，皆工之所不材也。

translations.literal: Silver with copper then blackens; copper with tin then flakes; pure copper long steeped then the belly rots and leaks—all what craftsmen reject.
translations.idiomatic: Silver with copper then blackens; copper with tin then flakes; pure copper long steeped then the belly rots and leaks—all what craftsmen reject.

sentences.zh: 《景表議》曰：

translations.literal: The Memorial on the Gnomon says:
translations.idiomatic: The Memorial on the Gnomon says:

translations.literal: The Memorial on the Gnomon says:
translations.idiomatic: The Memorial on the Gnomon says:

sentences.zh: 步景之法，惟定南北爲難。

translations.literal: The method of stepping shadows—only fixing south and north is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The method of stepping shadows—only fixing south and north is hard.

sentences.zh: 古法置槷爲規，識日出之景與日入之景。

translations.literal: Ancient method set a gnomon as compass, marking the sun's rising shadow and setting shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient method set a gnomon as compass, marking the sun's rising shadow and setting shadow.

sentences.zh: 晝參諸日中之景，夜考之極星。

translations.literal: By day compare with the noon shadow, by night examine the pole star.
translations.idiomatic: By day compare with the noon shadow, by night examine the pole star.

sentences.zh: 極星不當天中，而候景之法取晨夕景之最長者規之，兩表相去中折以參驗，最短之景爲日中。

translations.literal: The pole star is not at heaven's center; yet the shadow-observing method takes the longest morning and evening shadows to compass them; the two tables distanced, folded in half to verify—the shortest shadow is noon.
